[PDF Version](https://ir.arhaus.com/node/10291/pdf)


BOSTON HEIGHTS, Ohio, Nov. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Arhaus, Inc. (“Arhaus” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: ARHS), a premium home furnishing brand known for responsibly sourced, artisan-crafted products and heirloom-quality design, reported third quarter results for the period ended September 30, 2026.


**Third Quarter** **2026** **Highlights** *Compared to the third quarter of 2025:*


- **Net revenue** increased 6.8% to $368 million
- **Gross margin** increased 8.2% to $144 million
- **Selling, general and administrative expenses** increased 14.8% to $134 million
- **Net and comprehensive income** decreased 36.0% to $8 million
- **Adjusted EBITDA** decreased 12.3% to $27 million
- **Comparable Delivered Sales** (1) increased 2.6%
- **Comparable Written Sales** (2) increased 13.9%


**John Reed, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer, said** :


“For 40 years, Arhaus has been defined by exceptional craftsmanship, timeless design, and distinctive products. Our continued investment in compelling new collections and expanded customization is resonating with clients, as reflected in third-quarter Comparable Written Sales(2) growth of 13.9%. As we celebrate our 40th anniversary, we remain excited about the opportunity to bring our unique product offering to more clients and build on our momentum.”


**Michael Lee, Chief Financial Officer, said:**


“We are pleased with our third-quarter performance, which reflects strong client demand, disciplined execution, and continued progress across our strategic priorities. Our investments in our people, infrastructure, and technology are strengthening our foundation and positioning Arhaus for sustainable, profitable long-term growth. I want to thank our entire Arhaus team for their dedication, passion, and continued commitment to delivering an exceptional client experience.”


**Business Highlights**


Third quarter net revenue was $368 million, an increase of 6.8% year-over-year and within the Company’s guidance range.


Comparable Delivered Sales(1) increased 2.6% in the third-quarter, within the Company’s guidance range, bringing year-to-date Comparable Delivered Sales(1) to 1.8%. Comparable Written Sales(2) increased 13.9% in the third-quarter, bringing year-to-date Comparable Written Sales(2) to 6.7%.


**Showroom Highlights**


At the end of the third quarter of 2026, Arhaus operated 109 Showrooms across 31 states. During the quarter, the Company completed 2 Total Showroom Projects(3), including 1 relocated Showroom in Charlotte, North Carolina, and 1 renovated Showroom in Atlanta, Georgia.


Notable updates include:


- **Charlotte, North Carolina** – The Company relocated its Traditional Showroom in The Village at SouthPark. Spanning approximately 35,000-square-feet, the freestanding location is now Arhaus’ second-largest Traditional Showroom after Pasadena, California, offering an expanded destination to experience the brand’s artisan-crafted collections, and personalized interior design services.


For 2026, the Company continues to expect to complete approximately 10 to 14 Total Showroom Projects(3), consisting of 4 to 6 new openings and 6 to 8 relocations, renovations, or expansions, representing Net Unit Growth(4) of mid-single-digits for the year.


**Balance Sheet and Liquidity**


As of September 30, 2026, the Company reported the following:


- No long-term debt.
- Cash and cash equivalents totaled $318 million, a 25.5% increase from December 31, 2025.
- Net merchandise inventory of $360 million, a 6.4% increase from December 31, 2025.
- Client deposits of $325 million, a 37.7% increase from December 31, 2025.
- Net cash provided by operating activities totaled $173 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.
- Net cash used in investing activities was $58 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. Company-funded capital expenditures(5) were $46 million and landlord contributions were $12 million.


**Outlook**


The Company is raising its full-year Net revenue and Comparable Delivered Sales(1) outlook, reflecting strength in client demand and momentum in Comparable Written Sales(2). The Company is maintaining its full-year Net Income and Adjusted EBITDA outlook, following an increase last quarter, reflecting continued fuel and transportation cost pressures and the strategic investment into expanded marketing initiatives to support future growth. The Company remains focused on disciplined expense management, operational efficiencies, and long-term profitable growth.

(1) **Comparable Delivered Sales** is a key performance indicator and is defined as the year-over-year percentage change of the dollar value of orders delivered (based on purchase price), net of the dollar value of returns (based on amount credited to client), from our comparable Showrooms and eCommerce, including through our catalogs and other mailings.
(2) **Comparable Written Sales** is a key performance indicator and is defined as the year-over-year percentage change of written sales from our comparable Showrooms and eCommerce, including through our catalogs and other mailings.
(3) **Total Showroom Projects** is defined as the number of Showroom projects completed during the period, including new Showroom openings, relocations, remodels, and expansions. The Company considers all Showroom projects integral to its long-term growth strategy, with each evaluated based on strategic relevance and expected return on investment.
(4) **Net Unit Growth** reflects the percentage change in total Showroom count during the period, calculated as new Showroom openings net of Showroom closures or relocations that do not increase total unit count.
(5) **Company-funded capital expenditures** is defined as total net cash used in investing activities less landlord contributions.
(6) U.S. GAAP net income (loss).
(7) We have not reconciled guidance for Adjusted EBITDA to the corresponding GAAP financial measure because we do not provide guidance for the various reconciling items. These items include, but are not limited to, future share-based compensation expense, income taxes, interest income, and transaction costs. We are unable to provide guidance for these reconciling items because we cannot determine their probable significance, as certain items are outside of our control and cannot be reasonably predicted due to the fact that these items could vary significantly from period to period. Accordingly, reconciliations to the corresponding GAAP financial measure is not available without unreasonable effort

**About Arhaus**


Founded in 1986 by Chief Executive Officer John Reed and his father, Arhaus is a premium home furnishings brand built on a simple idea: furniture and décor should be responsibly sourced, lovingly made, and built to last. Arhaus operates a vertically integrated model, designing and sourcing products directly from skilled artisans and carefully selected manufacturing partners around the world, including domestic upholstery production at its own North Carolina manufacturing facility. This approach enables Arhaus to offer a highly exclusive and customizable assortment of heirloom-quality furniture and décor designed to be used and enjoyed for generations.


With more than 100 Showroom locations across the United States, Arhaus’ integrated omni-channel model connects every client touchpoint, from Showroom and interior design to eCommerce and catalog, allowing Arhaus to meet clients wherever and however they choose to shop while delivering a highly personalized client-first experience from discovery through delivery.


For more information, please visit[www.arhaus.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=4yOcOSHi_j7asPOvnq5qVocclytevlU4eU2fWGynnkC5jcTDTJ6eckTVNxPc9VQyepEDwXcOuFDI0W7t5VPoow==) .

**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


In addition to the results provided in accordance with U.S. GAAP, this press release and related tables include adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of net revenue, and Free Cash Flow, which present operating results on an adjusted basis.


We use non-GAAP measures to help assess the performance of our business, identify trends affecting our business, formulate business plans and make strategic decisions. In addition to our results determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP, we believe that providing these non-GAAP financial measures is useful to our investors as they present an informative supplemental view of our results from period to period by removing the effect of non-recurring items. However, our inclusion of these adjusted measures should not be construed as an indication that our future results will be unaffected by unusual or infrequent items or that the items for which we have made adjustments are unusual or infrequent or will not recur. These non-U.S. GAAP measures are not a substitute for, or superior to, measures of financial performance prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Because not all companies use identical calculations, the presentations of these measures may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures of other companies and can differ significantly from company to company. These measures should only be read together with the corresponding U.S. GAAP measures. Please refer to the reconciliations of adjusted EBITDA and Free Cash Flow to the most directly comparable financial measures prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP below.
